key_insight: One expert directing parallel LLM agents ported CompCert’s verified compiler core from Rocq to Lean in approximately six weeks while retaining formal correctness guarantees.
engineering_relevance: Dependency-aware agent workflows can support large verified-software migrations and subsequent compiler optimization with limited human technical direction.
method: Partition the migration along dependency boundaries.
Audit translated definitions and theorem statements before reconstructing proofs.
Rebuild proofs in parallel against stable interfaces.
evidence_signal: The port discharged all 4,908 recorded proof obligations without project-specific axioms; under matched 24-active-hour budgets, agent-produced Lean and Rocq candidates reduced generated-program runtime by 11.7% and 2.3%, respectively, across 29 small-tests programs.
watch_item: Performance results cover only 29 small-tests programs, so gains may not generalize to larger production workloads.
paper_title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
